verdict.rationale: Bun's package manager presents itself as a drop-in replacement for npm, yarn and pnpm. Its verbs mirror the incumbents': `bun install`, `add`, `remove`, `update`, `outdated`, `why`, `info`, `link`, `publish`, `pm pack` (following `npm pack` rules) and `bunx`. Familiar conventions also carry over: `-g`, `--frozen-lockfile`, `--filter`, `workspace:*`, npm `overrides` and Yarn `resolutions`, and a community user called the switching cost zero. Missing for 10: an official command-mapping or alias guide from npm/yarn/pnpm syntax to Bun, independent hands-on confirmation of full flag parity, and Bun not running dependency lifecycle scripts like `postinstall` by default, which breaks npm's convention.
